oneLine: Real progress in the close frames: flash now paints the S5 facades, S4 reads as a lit, varied town, and the S7 Moab layers have lit slopes. But every wide canonical frame (S1, S2, S3, S6, S7) is still a featureless beige plane with a game-board town on it. The new villa quarter is a perfect elliptical 'racetrack' loop, the far town still reads as silver glitter, and roads are blue-black tubes. Competent indie, not yet next to CoH3, TW:WH3 or CS2.
strengths: The console is clean in all 7 shots (no env or vfx errors). The whole frame is 77-94 draw calls and 1.06-1.11 M triangles, so the env share stays inside the 120 calls / 1.1 M limit.

S5-street: the shared flash term works. The intercept overhead now warms the facing walls and roofs instead of leaving black silhouettes, and the window variety (blinds, dark floors, cool and warm temperatures, balcony depth) is close to Cities: Skylines II night windows. This is the best frame.

S4-alert reads as a lived-in town at tactical zoom. Sodium pools now pop against darker lots, there is a mix of slabs, towers, low commercial blocks and red-roof houses, plus palms, parked-car courts, crosswalks and a green shelter glow. In vocabulary, it is the closest frame to a CoH3 night map.

S7: the Moab range is now a surface with lit west slopes and gullies, and the farther ridges are paler and hazier, so the atmospheric perspective is no longer inverted. Salt rim, Dead Sea band and shore lights give TW:WH3-style plate separation for the first time. The warm light-pollution dome over Arad reads in S7 and on the S1 horizon.

The S3 battery pad is no longer a blue swimming pool: it is a matte warm apron, the road shoulders are narrower, and lane paint and lamp heads read. The S3 ridge line on the horizon has relief and haze.
The S2 near-desert smudges and ink-blot shrubs from R2 are gone, and the ground has a warm, consistent ochre albedo under cool moonlight with no banding in the sky.

issues.area: town layout / skyline from the RTS camera (S2, S6)
issues.text: At the default tactical camera, Arad is still an octagon of equal square blocks with glowing tan outlines on a blank plain. The new 'villa quarter' to the east is a perfect ellipse of red-roofed houses around a loop lane, with a straight spur in. From above it reads as a racetrack or a stadium, which is the most procedural-looking object in the frame. The west lobe is a thin Y of sheds, and the walled compounds are lone square tiles. In S6 the town is still a band of silver-white boxes, not warm windows on dark massing. Next to Age of Empires IV and CS2 overviews, this is a first-glance prototype tell.
issues.fix: In src/env/outskirts.js lines 68-79, replace the parametric ellipse loop (cx+cos*rx, cz+sin*rz with 20 even samples) with an irregular organic lane: jitter the radius per sample by ±25-35%, open the loop into 2-3 cul-de-sacs, and add 2-3 cross lanes so that houses fill the interior instead of lining a ring. In world/layout.js (building part only), remove some of the octagon-perimeter street segments, or drop their lights, and push building lots past the perimeter at 3-4 points, so the core edge is ragged. In src/env/town.js line 446, the far-facade darkening mix(1.0, 0.5, smoothstep(1400, 5000, d)) is too weak to read at S6 distance: go to 0.25 and start at 900, and also reduce the moon/hemisphere response, not just the albedo (S6 facades are clearly specular/ambient-lit silver). Cut the tan 'walk' strip brightness on the block perimeters by about 40% at distance so the blocks stop reading as outlined tiles.

issues.text: Three of the seven canonical frames are about 60% empty flat beige plane. S1's foreground is a uniform featureless surface, with nothing between the camera and the town. In S3 the plateau to the horizon is a single flat tone with no rocks, wadis, scrub or relief. In S7 the bottom two-thirds is an even grey-brown sheet. The claimed shrubs and desert-pavement mottling are invisible at these distances. Iron Harvest and CoH3 never leave half the screen as a flat albedo, and TW:WH3 foregrounds always carry rock, relief or vegetation.
issues.fix: In src/env/terrain.js, scale the mottling to the view. Add a large-scale (wavelength 300-800 m) low-frequency albedo and roughness variation at ±20%: dark hamada gravel against pale loess, with a ridged-noise mask. Cut 10-30 m-deep, 50-150 m-wide meandering wadi channels into the heightfield on the plateau, so that grazing moonlight produces visible relief and shadows. Raise the near-camera BH bump amplitude so that S3's foreground shows rills. Scatter instanced low rock outcrops and acacia clusters (a few hundred instances, merged) along the wadi beds, so S1 and S3 have foreground silhouettes.

issues.text: The regional roads render as blue-black tubes that look raised above the ground. In S7 the Route 31 line and the long diagonal look like cables lying on the desert. In S1 a dark navy rope curves in from the left. The town.js comment says far asphalt should read as a pale grey line, but in the shots it is the darkest value in the scene, and it is cold blue against the warm ground.
issues.fix: In src/env/town.js around line 164 (the far-asphalt branch) and the regional road material in terrain.js or city.js: blend road albedo toward the terrain colour by smoothstep(800, 4000, dist), up to 70%. Give it the same warm-emissive and fog/inscatter treatment as the terrain, so it does not stay cold navy under the moon. Clamp the ribbon's minimum on-screen width rather than letting it alias into a thick dark stroke, and check the y offset (0.35) and normals so it does not read as a raised tube at grazing angles.

issues.text: The plateau still ends in a ruler-straight horizontal line against the far ridge in S3 and S6. There is no visible drop, rift haze or cliff band, so the mid-ground layer (escarpment and Dead Sea) is missing from both frames, and the composition goes straight from flat ground to the ridge. In S6 the far ridge is a flat uniform band, and above it is a huge empty black sky.
issues.fix: In src/env/terrain.js, perturb the plateau rim with 1-3 km-wavelength noise (±300-600 m in x) and add 2-3 spur headlands, so the edge silhouette is broken. In src/env/atmosphere.js, add a pale rift-haze layer (extra density for y below the plateau rim inside the rift x-range) so that a bright band sits between the plateau edge and Moab. In S6, let the light-pollution and horizon glow extend higher (the gradient dies at about 25% of the frame height) so the upper sky is not flat black.

issues.text: Roofs are still flat grey slabs with a single box and a red dot, repeated across buildings. The rooftop clutter claimed to be bigger is not readable at S4 zoom. The block interiors are flat brown, and the scrub decals are square yellow-green tiles with hard edges. The battery vehicles in S3 are simple box clusters.
issues.fix: In src/env/city.js, cluster 3-8 solar heaters and black tanks per slab roof at about 1.5× scale, add a parapet lip and stairwell head-house variation, and drop the red-dot box from most roofs. Give the decals a noisy radial alpha falloff and random rotation. In src/env/batteries.js, add a cab, wheels, a raised launcher box at an angle and a radar face to the launchers.

benchmarkNotes: Company of Heroes 3 night maps: S4 is now in the right ballpark for vocabulary and light pools, but the roofs and lots are too uniform; it is close to a CoH3 town at a glance, not under scrutiny. Iron Harvest: the sky, crescent halo and warm dome are in the right spirit, but there is no volumetric depth between layers in S1 or S3, and the foreground is empty where Iron Harvest would put rocks, fences and silhouettes. Total War: Warhammer III vistas: S7's Moab surfaces with haze stepping are the first real TW:WH3-style layering, but S3 and S6 still cut flat plain to ridge with no escarpment, and the foreground of S7 is a blank sheet crossed by cable-like roads. Cities: Skylines II night: S5 windows and flash-lit facades hold up well, but the overview frames (S2, S6) show a tiled octagon, a racetrack-shaped villa loop and silver far facades, nothing like a CS2 skyline at distance. Age of Empires IV high camera: S2 remains the procedural giveaway. Net: two frames (S4, S5) approach a 6-7, but four of the seven canonical frames would sit visibly below the references in a store-page row, so 5.
